Those states live in hypotheses/hypotheses.json, result/probe-report.json, proposals/mechanism-changes.json and proposals/strategy-proposals.json respectively.
retrieval_method: HTTPS GET of raw content at an immutable commit id, resolved through the public GitHub API. Tag names were resolved to commit ids first so that no claim depends on a mutable ref. Rendered documentation pages were not used as evidence; the versioned source of those pages was.

external_claims.verbatim_excerpt:
fetch-depth:
    description: 'Number of commits to fetch. 0 indicates all history for all branches and tags.'
    default: 1
external_claims.claim: The fetch-depth input of actions/checkout defaults to 1, so a workflow that does not set it receives a shallow checkout containing a single commit.

external_claims.verbatim_excerpt: Only a single commit is fetched by default, for the ref/SHA that triggered the workflow. Set `fetch-depth: 0` to fetch all history for all branches and tags.
external_claims.claim: The default checkout carries only the triggering commit; complete history is available only when fetch-depth is set to 0.

external_claims.ref_resolved_from: github/docs default branch head at read time
external_claims.verbatim_excerpt: When this workflow is triggered, {% data variables.product.prodname_dotcom %} provisions a new virtual machine for each job.
external_claims.claim: Each job on a GitHub-hosted runner receives a newly provisioned virtual machine, so no local state survives from a previous job or run.

external_claims.artefact: GitHub Docs source, Actions variables reference
external_claims.verbatim_excerpt: | `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` | The default working directory on the runner for steps, and the default location of your repository when using the [`checkout`](https://github.com/actions/checkout) action. For example, `/home/runner/work/my-repo-name/my-repo-name`. |
external_claims.claim: The repository lives at a runner-assigned absolute path exposed as GITHUB_WORKSPACE, and the runner supplies its own temporary directory as RUNNER_TEMP; neither path is stable across environments.

external_claims.verbatim_excerpt: description: "Set up a specific version of Python and add the command-line tools to the PATH."
external_claims.claim: A bare 'python' command on a runner resolves because actions/setup-python placed it on PATH; the spelling is a property of the job, not of the repository.

external_claims.verbatim_excerpt:
-B

   If given, Python won't try to write ``.pyc`` files on the import of source modules.  See also :envvar:`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE`.

-I

   Run Python in isolated mode. This also implies :option:`-E`, :option:`-P` and :option:`-s` options.

   In isolated mode :data:`sys.path` contains neither the script's directory nor the user's site-packages directory. All ``PYTHON*`` environment variables are ignored, too.
external_claims.claim: Only -B suppresses bytecode writing on the command line. Isolated mode -I ignores every PYTHON* environment variable, and it implies -P, which stops CPython prepending the working directory to sys.path.

repository_claims.verbatim_excerpt:
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Run dependency-free contract tests
        run: python -I -m unittest discover -s workstreams/po03/tests -p 'test_*.py' -v
repository_claims.claim: The PO-03 contracts workflow does request complete history and does set up Python, and its test command uses isolated mode with a working-directory-relative start directory.

exclusions: Rendered docs.github.com HTML pages were read only to locate content and were not used as evidence, because a rendered page carries no immutable identifier. The versioned Markdown source in github/docs was cited instead.
actions/runner-images was not consulted. Preinstalled-software inventories were outside this unit's hypotheses and would have added unverified breadth.

No practitioner blog, forum thread or social post was admitted. Every claim here has either an immutable upstream commit or an immutable repository path, so no claim rests on a mutable or unversioned surface.

GitHub Enterprise Server and self-hosted runner behaviour was not tested. Self-hosted runners can reuse a workspace between jobs, which would change the conclusions; recorded as out of scope rather than assumed equivalent.
Windows and macOS runners were not tested. All reproductions ran on Linux.

not_supported.subject: A live GitHub Actions workflow run for this unit
not_supported.boundary: Dispatching a workflow run would be an external mutation of the repository's CI surface and would require creating or modifying a pull request, both of which this unit is forbidden to do. The harness therefore reconstructs the runner's checkout and environment shape locally from the pinned actions/checkout and setup-python manifests, and every conclusion is labelled CI-equivalent rather than CI-observed.

not_supported.subject: Byte counts and digests for the two github/docs Markdown sources
not_supported.boundary: Those two files were read for their verbatim claim text only and their transfer digests were not captured at read time. Rather than compute a value after the fact and present it as a read-time observation, the field is left NOT_SUPPORTED; the immutable commit id plus path is sufficient to re-derive both.
